scope: Theorem 1.2 (Sharp boundary mass and annealed chord laws) of the manuscript “Disk transfer representations and confined bridge mass” (preprints/Disk-transfer-representations-and-confined-bridge-mass-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 237 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d64dc634fe49d994), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 4. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The following conclusions hold as the indicated scale tends to infinity. 1. The arch kernel is nonincreasing and h(m) ≍ m−5/4 , μ(height > R) ≍ μ(diameter > R) ≍ R−1/4 . 2. For every sufficiently large fixed C, normalize μ either on R ≤ diameter ≤ CR, or on height ≥ R and diameter ≤ CR. Under either law, Eℓ = R4/3+o(1). 3. Let DR = {y : ei · y < R, i = 0, 1, 2}, IR = {v a lattice vertex : ei · v < (1 − ε)R, i = 0, 1, 2}, where R ∈ 1 2 + 3 2Z and ε > 0 is sufficiently small and fixed. Sum critical chord weights over the ordered pair of boundary ports and normalize on chords visiting IR. Uniformly for v ∈ IR, their visit probability is R−2/3+o(1). The expected total number of visited vertices, and the expected number in IR, are both R4/3+o(1).
